name: Mozilla Firefox (en-US)
author: Mozilla Foundation
summary: Mozilla Firefox is free and open source software, built by a community of thousands from all over the world.
description: Firefox Browser, also known as Mozilla Firefox or simply Firefox, is a free and open-source web browser developed by the Mozilla Foundation and its subsidiary, the Mozilla Corporation. Firefox uses the Gecko layout engine to render web pages, which implements current and anticipated web standards. In 2017, Firefox began incorporating new technology under the code name Quantum to promote parallelism and a more intuitive user interface. Firefox is officially available for Windows 7 or newer, macOS, and Linux. Its unofficial ports are available for various Unix and Unix-like operating systems including FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, illumos, and Solaris Unix.

Version 160.0, first offered to Release channel users on November 10, 2026

New
- The Picture-in-Picture player now has a playback speed setting, with options ranging from 0.25x to 2.0x speed. The setting appears only when the player window is medium-sized or larger.

- Mini Window moves a tab or a selected part of a page into an always-on-top window while browsing. We’d appreciate feedback on Mozilla Connect as we develop and improve this early version of the feature.

- History entries can now be dragged from the sidebar to the tab strip to open them in new tabs.
- The address bar context menu now shows "Paste and Search" instead of "Paste and Go" when the copied text is a search term rather than a web address.
- Pages saved as PDF now make mathematical content (MathML) accessible to assistive technology such as screen readers.
- Websites that repeatedly ask to handle email (mailto:) and other links can now be blocked with a new “Never allow” button, and blocked sites can be managed in Settings.
- Firefox now plays Matroska (MKV) files with FLAC, MP3, or PCM audio.
- WebGL content on macOS is now rendered using Apple's Metal graphics API, which can improve performance on some sites.
- In Smart Window, Organize Tabs is now available in French. Firefox can suggest groups of related open tabs and name each group in French.
  This feature is part of a progressive roll out.
  What is a progressive roll out?
  Certain new Firefox features are released gradually. This means some users will see the feature before everyone does. This approach helps to get early feedback to catch bugs and improve behavior quickly, meaning more Firefox users overall have a better experience.

Fixed
- Fixed the first character typed into the address bar or search bar sometimes being lost when typing quickly right after clicking into it.
- Increased the contrast between the domain name and the rest of the address in the address bar, making it easier to see which website is open.
- Fixed Firefox freezing for several seconds when signing in to intranet sites that use NTLM or Kerberos (Negotiate) authentication.
- Fixed double-tapping or long-pressing a word to select it, and tapping to place the cursor, not working near the cursor in text fields.
- Fixed links opened in the background from other apps on macOS, such as RSS readers, bringing Firefox to the foreground.
- Fixed downloaded files on macOS sometimes opening in the wrong application instead of the default one set in Finder.
- Fixed simultaneous downloads on macOS never finishing when Firefox is set to ask where to save files. Only the first file showed a save dialog.
- Restored meaningful filenames and the usual save workflow for PDFs opened in Preview from the macOS print dialog.
- Various security fixes.

Version 159.0, first offered to Release channel users on October 27, 2026

New
- Sharing on macOS now uses the native macOS share picker, which shows a preview of the page and recent contacts alongside AirDrop, Messages, and other apps. Several selected tabs can also be shared at once.

- Saved passwords are now available from the sidebar by default, without having to add the Passwords tool first.

- Smart Window can now watch pages for changes such as price drops or restocks. Type /watch in the chat to set one up, and Firefox sends a desktop notification when it finds a match. Watches can be managed from the Tasks button in the toolbar or the about:smartwindowtasks page.
  This feature is part of a progressive roll out.
  What is a progressive roll out?
  Certain new Firefox features are released gradually. This means some users will see the feature before everyone does. This approach helps to get early feedback to catch bugs and improve behavior quickly, meaning more Firefox users overall have a better experience.

Fixed
- Fixed the file upload dialog opening in the last folder a file was saved to, such as Downloads, instead of the folder last used for uploads.
- Fixed memory usage growing rapidly when sites such as the Zoom web app were left open in a minimized window.
- Fixed some videos displaying incorrectly on Windows when NVIDIA RTX Video HDR is enabled.
- Fixed bookmarks not being imported from Google Chrome profiles that are signed in to a Google account.
- Fixed the Replace button in Apple Writing Tools on macOS inserting the clipboard contents instead of the rewritten text on some sites, such as Gmail.
- Fixed long drop-down lists on web pages sometimes showing blank space in place of the last options until the list was scrolled.
- Fixed some sites, such as Slack, failing to load instead of falling back to HTTP/2 when the site rejected an HTTP/3 request.
- Fixed Firefox using excessive memory on Linux with AMD graphics when viewing map or place results on sites such as ChatGPT.
- Fixed quick gamepad button presses sometimes being missed in web games on macOS.
- Fixed tabs sometimes detaching into a new window when clicked on Linux with Wayland.
- Fixed menus and panels fading in on Windows and Linux when animation effects are turned off in the operating system.
- Various security fixes.

Changed
- On macOS, apps that sign in through the default browser, such as ChatGPT, now open their sign-in page in Firefox instead of Safari when Firefox is the default browser.
- The AI chatbot's Summarize page option now sends the page's address to the chatbot provider instead of the page's text, so long pages are no longer cut short to a partial summary.
- Open tabs can now be searched with a keyboard shortcut: Ctrl+Shift+A on Windows and Linux, Cmd+Shift+A on macOS. The Extensions and Themes shortcut is now Ctrl+Shift+F on Windows and Linux, and Cmd+Shift+E on macOS. These shortcuts can be changed in about:keyboard.
- Web addresses written in the Javanese, Balinese, Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics, and N'Ko scripts are now displayed in their own script instead of as encoded "xn--" text.

Enterprise
- For Firefox Enterprise updates and fixes, see the Firefox Enterprise release notes. For policy changes, see the Firefox admin docs changelog.

Developer
- The Web Console now allows let, const, and class variables to be declared again, so a snippet can be edited and re-run without a redeclaration error.

Web Platform
- Firefox now supports scroll-driven animations, so CSS animations and Web Animations API animations can progress with the scroll position of a container or with an element's visibility as it scrolls into view. This adds the animation-timeline, scroll-timeline, view-timeline, and animation-range properties and the ScrollTimeline and ViewTimeline interfaces.
- Firefox now supports scoped custom element registries. A registry created with the CustomElementRegistry() constructor is separate from the global window.customElements registry, so custom elements that share a tag name can coexist on the same page.
- On compatible devices, WebGL now supports the EXT_clip_control and EXT_texture_mirror_clamp_to_edge extensions and WebGL 2 supports EXT_texture_norm16.
- The Sanitizer API now sanitizes HTML as it is parsed rather than afterwards, so custom element constructors no longer run for elements the sanitizer removes.

- Fixed the Vertical Tabs sidebar not reappearing when the cursor moves to the edge of the screen in full screen mode.

New

Fixed
- Fixed text disappearing in Microsoft 365 Word Online and other web apps on Linux when typing with certain keyboard layouts.
- Fixed an unnecessary paste confirmation appearing when using the keyboard shortcut to paste without formatting in Google Docs.
- Firefox now recovers from the toolbar and tab strip being left unresponsive when the platform fails to end a tab drag session.
- Fixed text inside buttons not being selectable or copyable, which prevented copying direct messages on X and comments on YouTube.
- Fixed live audio streams such as internet radio stopping when playing in the background.
- Fixed the sound indicator disappearing from a tab that was moved to another window, leaving no way to see or mute what was playing.
- Fixed Firefox preventing Linux systems from going to sleep after a long browsing session.
- Fixed full screen content being letterboxed on MacBooks with a camera notch, most visibly when watching video.
- Fixed arrow-key and Page Up/Down scrolling not working on some pages with embedded content from other sites.
- Fixed characters from some less common scripts appearing as empty boxes on web pages on Windows.
- Fixed WebCodecs VideoEncoder hanging on macOS when encoding a VideoFrame in NV12 format.
- Various security fixes.

Changed
- Firefox now limits CSS to 75 levels of nested blocks and functions, preventing crashes that extremely deep nesting can cause under some circumstances. More deeply nested rules and values no longer parse.
- Firefox now uses firefox-portal-detection.com instead of detectportal.firefox.com to detect captive portals and check network connectivity, so network allowlists referencing the old domain need updating.
- Firefox now opens mailto: links only in response to an explicit user action, so pages can no longer launch the default mail client unprompted.
- PDFs smaller than the paper size can now be enlarged to fill the sheet when printing, by setting the scale above 100%.

Enterprise

Developer
- The Rules View now offers toggles to emulate the prefers-reduced-motion media feature. Emulation options have also moved into a new panel behind the at-rules (@) button.
- The Debugger in Developer Tools now has a keyboard shortcut, Ctrl+Alt+B (Cmd+Alt+B on macOS), to enable or disable all breakpoints at once.
- The JSON Viewer now displays JSON Lines (JSONL/NDJSON) documents, including inline errors for invalid lines.
- Fixed the Storage panel showing cookies from private windows, containers, and other partitions alongside the inspected page's own cookies.
- Uncaught non-Error exceptions now list their property names in the Console instead of showing only Object.

Web Platform
- The CSS attr() function now supports values of any type, so authors can use attribute values in any property rather than only as strings in the content property.
- Firefox now supports the progress() CSS function.
- Firefox now supports the alpha() CSS function. This is a relative color function that can be used to modify just the alpha component of a given color.
- Firefox now supports the Promise.allKeyed and Promise.allSettledKeyed methods from the await dictionary proposal, which take an object of promises and resolve to an object of results with the same keys.
- Firefox now supports the WebAssembly Compact Import Section proposal, which can reduce the size of WebAssembly modules with many imports.
- Firefox now supports the WebAssembly Wide Arithmetic proposal, which adds 128-bit arithmetic instructions for better performance in cryptography and arbitrary-precision math.
- Firefox now supports QUIC version 2 (RFC 9369) for HTTP/3 connections, and uses it when the server selects it through compatible version negotiation (RFC 9368).
- Support for the non-standard ::-webkit-scrollbar pseudo-element, added in Firefox 153, is now limited to a small list of sites rather than applying universally.
- SVG <a> elements now expose the same URL properties as HTML links, including protocol, host, pathname, and search.
- SVGGraphicsElement.getBBox() now honors its options argument, so bounding boxes can include stroke, markers, and clipping.
- The font-width property is now supported as the standard name for font-stretch.
- A dynamic import() that fails due to a network or HTTP error is no longer cached as a failure in the module map, so retrying the same specifier can now succeed.

Web Platform
- Added support for a post-quantum key exchange mechanism for TLS 1.3 (mlkem768x25519) which secures communications against advanced / long-term threats.
- Added support for Certificate Compression which reduces the size and increases the speed of a TLS handshake.

- The requestVideoFrameCallback() method is now available on the HTMLVideoElement interface. This method enables developers to perform efficient operations on each video frame.
- The getCapabilities method allows applications to gather the media capabilities supported for the live MediaStreamTrack.
- The fetchpriority attribute enables web developers to optimize resource loading by specifying the relative priority of resources to be fetched by the browser. It accepts three values: auto (default priority), low (lower priority), high (higher priority). It can be specified on script, link, img elements, on the RequestInit parameter of the fetch() method and Link response headers. The HTML specification leaves the detailed interpretation of this attribute up to implementers. Firefox will typically use it to increase or decrease the urgency parameter of HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 requests.

  This feature is part of a progressive roll out.
  What is a progressive roll out?
  Certain new Firefox features are released gradually. This means some users will see the feature before everyone does. This approach helps to get early feedback to catch bugs and improve behavior quickly, meaning more Firefox users overall have a better experience.
